Seven shelves, one subject.

The library is young and it will stay narrow. One subject, covered properly: practice real estate, from first lease to last sale. Every piece below is ready to read, organized by the decision in front of you.

The Ownership Decision

Rent, buy, or a structure in between. The math, the tradeoffs, and how to evaluate any third path, including ours.

Rent, buy, or wait. The real math for a practice owner.

You've seen the 30-year spreadsheet that proves buying wins. It's right, for people who aren't you yet. Where the math actually tips, and what to do in the years before it does.

How to tell whether a purchase option is real.

Five terms decide it: who sets the price, when the valuation happens, what conditions attach, what happens if you pass, and whether it survives a practice sale. Interrogate any deal with them, Medre included.

Starting a Practice

Real estate choices in the first two years, when every dollar belongs in the practice and every signature follows you.

Why your first lease matters more than your logo.

The location decision compounds for a decade. The branding decision gets repainted in year three. How to weight your first-space choices accordingly.

Short lease or long lease when you don't know your market yet.

Flexibility has a price and commitment has a different one. A way to choose that starts with your two-year forecast, not the landlord's term sheet.

How much space do you really need for your first practice?

Too small feels cramped; too big strains cash flow for years. How to size your first space around workflow, not a square-foot guess.

Leases and Renewals

The documents practices actually sign, and the leverage hiding inside them.

How to handle a renewal when moving is not realistic.

Your landlord knows your relocation costs better than you do, and prices accordingly. What leverage you still have, and when the answer is renegotiating, relocating, or restructuring toward ownership.

The renewal clock starts two years early. Here's the calendar.

What to do at 24 months, 18, 12, and 6, so the negotiation starts before your landlord knows it has.

Buying a Building

Down payments, guarantees, appraisals, and debt. What ownership costs before it pays.

What a personal guarantee actually costs you.

The bank calls it standard. It's a claim on your house and on your next decision. What guaranteeing a commercial mortgage means before anything goes wrong.

When owning your first building is actually the cheaper move.

The cases where we'd tell you to skip us: real capital, a stable market, and a decade of certainty. How to know whether that's you.

Expansion and Site Selection

Second locations, outgrown space, and where to plant the next flag.

A simple way to think about expansion and real estate risk in the same breath.

A second location doubles your fixed costs before it doubles your revenue. How to sequence the space decision with the growth decision instead of after it.

Outgrowing your space: renovate, relocate, or restructure.

The walls are the symptom. How to tell whether the cure is a contractor, a mover, or a different deal on the building.

Sale-Leasebacks and Locked Equity

For owners wondering about the capital inside their walls, and how to free it without losing the building for good.

The sale-leaseback, explained for practice owners.

What selling your building and leasing it back actually trades away, what the buyer is counting on, and the one clause that decides whether you can ever get the building back.

How to read a sale-leaseback offer without getting boxed out of ownership.

The buyback terms matter more than the price. The clauses that decide whether you can ever get the building back, and the ones written so you can't.

Refinance or sale-leaseback: run both before signing either.

Two ways to free the capital in your walls, with different costs and different endings. A side-by-side worth running before either suitor is in the room.

Exit and Succession

What the building does to a practice sale, and what to ask your attorney long before one.

Does your building help or hurt your practice sale?

Buyers price your real estate arrangement whether you did or not. When ownership adds to the check, and when a bad lease subtracts from it.

What your estate attorney should ask about your real estate.

The building outlives the career. Questions worth raising with your attorney while the answers are still cheap.

Who writes this

Erika Christiansen, a licensed Colorado commercial real estate broker, and Steve Christiansen, MD, a practicing retina specialist and practice owner. Equal partners, investing in real estate since 2009. No ghostwriters, no content team.

Nothing here is legal, tax, accounting, financing, or investment advice. Bring your attorney and accountant to anything you sign, including anything from us.

Medre. The lease that ends in ownership.

MedRe Partners, LLC. We buy the building, you lease it at fair market rent plus a small premium, and a written option at year 5 or year 10 lets you buy at a price set by independent appraisal when you exercise. Founded by a commercial real estate broker and a practicing physician.
